description: A research_append write marking a plan item `completed` whose `record_type` has a known vocabulary (RECORD_TYPE_TERMS: probate, census, vital/vital_record, church/church_record, marriage, naturalization, obituary) when some log[] entry is attributed to it but NONE names a search of that type — the probate item closed off a deed/land search (ut_search_full_text_016/_020). Silent when an attributed entry matches the type, when nothing is attributed (the structural gate's job), when the record_type is outside the vocabulary, and for any status but completed. Replayed by planItemCompletionRecordTypeInvariants (research-append.ts), the content half of the completion check.
format: expect: fire | silent, judged for the plan item named by `write` (found in research.plans[].items). research.log holds the attributed entries. Every fire case carries a `shape`; a guard needs at least two distinct fire shapes and at least one silent case.

cases.why: A probate plan item marked completed whose only attributed log entry is a deed/land fulltext search — no probate term in tool/notes/query.

log.notes: 1 result in Pennsylvania Land Records (collectionId 2220359), Schuylkill

cases.why: A census plan item marked completed whose only attributed entry is a marriage search — no census term (census/household/dwelling/enumerat).

log.notes: Marriage of John Flynn to Mary Byrne, 1868

cases.why: An attributed entry names an estate search — the probate vocabulary matches.

log.notes: Estate inventory and appraisement of Thomas Flynn

cases.why: The attributed entry's query carries recordType: probate — the term appears in the serialized query.
record_type 'deed' is outside RECORD_TYPE_TERMS — structural check only, no content assertion.
Nothing is attributed to the item — the structural gate (planItemLogAttributionInvariants) owns this, not the content half.
Forward only — an item not ending at completed is never judged.
